4. The trial Court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 20-3-1994 decreed the suit on condition that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 would get the privilege of getting pre-empted the plaintiff's share under section 4 of the Partition Act if Taka 90,000 was deposited within 90 (ninety) days of the date of decree failing which the decree for partition was to be maintained. 

 5. On appeal being Title Appeal No. 53 of 1994, the appellate Court upon consideration of the evidence on record refused the claim of the benami as raised by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and held that the aid of section 4 of the Partition Act was not available in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and decreed the suit reversing the judgment of the trial Court. 

 8. The High Court Division found that the suit land under partition was not a dwelling house and, as such, section 4 of the Partition Act was not applicable in the case as claimed by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of the suit. The High Court Division also found that the trial Court rightly decided the matter in controversy and hence did not commit any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the judgment and decree.
